characters.description: Team 34's rune mage, providing barriers and explosives. Claire also sets an early rule against using Ilea's healing for injuries a teammate can recover from without help.
characters.name: Claire

characters.description: A former Riverwatch librarian whose knowledge helped Ilea understand Elos. Maria has been held in a rune-lined, mana-draining prison until Edwin, Felicia, and Aliana break her free.
characters.name: Maria

characters.description: An elite Redleaf warrior and Ilea's former conditional ally in matters involving Taleen ruins. Edwin helps free Maria from a hidden prison and leaves with her while the group's conflict with his family escalates.
characters.name: Edwin Redleaf

characters.description: Edwin's sister, an elite wind mage and former conditional ally of Ilea. Felicia takes part in freeing Maria from a rune-lined cell and remains with the Redleaf group as it moves on.
characters.name: Felicia Redleaf

characters.description: An elite water mage allied with Edwin and Felicia. Aliana supports Maria immediately after the prison rescue, providing food and water as the weakened librarian recovers.
characters.name: Aliana

characters.description: The Shadow's Hand head librarian and an information broker. Dagon values Taleen artifacts, sells limited knowledge, and offers time-bounded confidentiality concerning the questions and objects brought to him.
characters.name: Dagon

characters.description: A Redleaf figure who held Maria in a hidden prison. After Edwin, Felicia, and Aliana free her, Arthur requests rapid assistance while hunters pursue the group.
characters.name: Arthur Redleaf

characters.description: A Shadow's Hand elder who privately recruits Dagon for a rapid coup against the guild's leader and supporters. He is preparing rune work and monster-summoning resources for the tournament gathering.
characters.name: Unnamed Shadow's Hand Elder

characters.description: The leader of a veteran Shadow's Hand squad returning from the west. Sulivhaan is a gravity mage who believes the recent elven attacks on human settlements show an unusual degree of coordination.
characters.name: Sulivhaan

characters.description: A survivor of Salia and Lily's father. Roland trains his surviving daughter to fight monsters because he considers combat skill necessary for their safety after the refugees reach a western Kral Kingdom city.
characters.name: Roland

characters.description: Roland's surviving daughter and a refugee from Salia. During her father's training, Lily kills a wounded horned lion with the black dagger Ilea gave her.
characters.name: Lily

characters.description: The cover name Ilea uses during the offshore expedition. By this point, Ilea has told Eve that she came to Elos from a world without magic.
characters.name: Lilith

characters.description: A young displaced mage found alone in a ruin. Cless says she comes from London and is searching for her father, whom she describes as a doctor.
characters.name: Cless

characters.description: A powerful unidentified mage with golden eyes who controls the barriers and cutting magic inside an offshore ruin. He ends a confrontation, removes selected research, entrusts Cless to the Shadow's Hand party, and teleports away.
characters.name: Unidentified Golden-Eyed Mage

characters.description: A female Shadow's Hand elder who directs the first response when concealed rune circles activate during the tournament. She orders the circles destroyed and fights the emerging demons with black-burning axes.
characters.name: Unnamed Female Shadow's Hand Elder

characters.description: A sapient Mind Weaver encountered in the Great Salt. The demon communicates telepathically, directs lesser demons, and bargains with Ilea and Trian for information while the stranded pair search for a route home.
characters.name: Mind Weaver

characters.description: The name Ilea gives the Mind Weaver allied with her and Trian. Weavy shares knowledge of ancient runes and joins their investigation of a vast steel facility, although trust within the alliance remains cautious.
characters.name: Weavy

characters.description: A Shadow's Hand elder who engineered the demon rifts and used an ancient facility in the Great Salt. Adam Strand claims the invasion was a test meant to strengthen the Hand, then refuses to explain his larger purpose.
characters.name: Adam Strand

characters.description: A Dawntree noble whom Ilea rescued before this book. Alice's earlier flight and her family's hostility remain relevant when Dawntree hunters seek Ilea in the belief that Alice may be traveling with her.
characters.name: Alice Forkspear

recaps.ending: The Shadow's Hand clears Ravenhall after Ilea kills Bane of the Deep and the defenders break the demons' Mind Weaver command, but the powerful winged demon escapes. Dagon and Sulivhaan negotiate cooperation with the Empire, giving the Hand a larger role in the city's reconstruction. Claire joins the new administration and takes responsibility for Cless. Trian plans to check on his family after learning that demon attacks have spread, while the Golden Lily remains tied to that family. Eve kills a poison druid during her separate investigation but leaves the fight critically wounded and without healing supplies, so her immediate safety is unresolved. Weavy proves his allegiance but is still feared by humans. Ilea leaves for Riverwatch with Kyrian and Weavy. Adam Strand remains missing, the one-way demon-spawn lake still requires containment, the winged demon remains at large, and the mysteries surrounding Aki, Taleen technology, Cless's father, and travel between Earth and Elos remain open.
recaps.in_short: Ilea joins the Shadow's Hand and helps turn Team 34 into a capable unit alongside Claire, Eve, Kyrian, and Trian. Their missions lead to Cless, a child apparently displaced from Earth, before a Hand elder's rune plot unleashes demons across Ravenhall. Ilea and Trian are stranded in the Great Salt, ally with a Mind Weaver whom Ilea names Weavy, and use an ancient facility to return after Ilea rejects a possible route to Earth in favor of Elos. They find Ravenhall fallen and reunite surviving Hand forces under Dagon and Sulivhaan. Ilea, her allies, and Weavy break the demons' command structure and retake the city, though a winged demon escapes. Claire enters Ravenhall's new Hand-Imperial administration and cares for Cless. Trian turns toward his family, Eve is critically wounded after killing a poison druid linked to her investigation, and Ilea departs toward Riverwatch with Kyrian and Weavy while Adam Strand and the wider demon crisis remain unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Ilea arrived in Elos from a nonmagical world and became an Azarinth battle-healer. Her fighting style combines close combat, exceptional resilience, and healing, allowing her to survive threats that would overwhelm most adventurers. Her travels brought her into contact with Taleen ruins and with Aki, a sentient dagger whose origin remains unclear. She formed conditional alliances with Edwin Redleaf, Felicia Redleaf, and Aliana, and gained knowledge from Maria, a Riverwatch librarian. Ilea also rescued Alice Forkspear, leaving unresolved hostility connected to the Dawntree noble's family. Refugees including Roland and his daughter Lily survived the destruction of Salia and moved west. By the start of this volume, Ilea has concealed her origin from most people, accumulated rare Taleen-linked equipment, and reached the strength needed to seek more structured work and training in Ravenhall.

Ilea pays to enter the Shadow's Hand as an initiate, choosing an arrangement that leaves her free to refuse work and depart. In the guild settlement beneath Ravenhall, Aki detects an unexplained presence in her apartment, while Ilea encounters signs of hidden violence and mind magic. Her evaluation demonstrates unusual durability, rapid healing, teleportation, and strong close-range attacks, earning her a place as Team 34's tank-healer. The new team consists of Kyrian, a reserved metal-and-curse mage; Trian, a noble lightning mage with draining abilities; Eve, a secretive illusionist and singer; and Claire, a rune mage who begins imposing tactical discipline. Their early sparring reveals both their power and their lack of trust. Ilea defeats Kyrian and Trian, while Claire counters Eve's mental attack with prepared runes. The bouts also begin building Ilea's resistance to lightning, curses, and draining magic. The Hand sets a three-month training program intended to turn the five specialists into a functioning field team.

Team 34's training exposes persistent tension but also begins drawing Ilea, Eve, and Kyrian together outside formal sessions. Claire assumes the role of tactician, Kyrian's debt and guarded past remain unexplained, and Trian gradually agrees to cooperate despite clashes over his noble status. Ilea studies monsters, healing, archery, and close combat while learning how to detect indirect signs of Eve's concealment. Elsewhere, Edwin, Felicia, and Aliana free Maria from a hidden, mana-draining prison, prompting hunters connected to the Redleaf family to pursue them. Ilea trades damaged Taleen armor to Dagon, the Hand's librarian, in exchange for confidentiality and information about teleportation, other realms, and the Redleaf conflict. The records offer claims of realm travelers but no explanation for Ilea's arrival. Team 34 then prepares for an extended exercise in the Hand's artificial underground training environment, with all five members finally assembled for group work.

After months of difficult drills, Team 34 begins its first field mission at a silver mine where several adventuring parties vanished. Death spirits overwhelm Claire, Kyrian, and Trian with mental attacks, but Eve protects the group while Ilea heals their minds. Their combined abilities reveal and destroy the spirits. During the battle Ilea reaches level 200 in her ash class and evolves it into Inheritor of Eternal Ash, greatly strengthening her body and ash control. Deeper in the mine, the team defeats a level-262 Lost Wanderer while protecting one another from further spirits. Ilea heals a wounded six-winged fae and lets it leave. The group determines that exposed soul shard ore drew the deadly creatures, recovers the missing victims, and returns control of the mine to its settlement. Their success earns full payment and confirms that the five initiates can now operate as a genuine team.

Now full Shadow's Hand members, Team 34 completes a series of assignments. They uncover a village blood-magic operation, rescue a traumatized child, kill the ritualist, and expose local conspirators who traded victims for payment from unknown nobles. They then destroy a harpy colony and join an offshore expedition, where Ilea survives a severe poison trap and the group helps kill a level-334 Stone Guardian. Ilea uses the cover name Lilith and tells Eve that she came from a world without magic. Beyond the guardian, a golden barrier controlled by an unidentified mage severs Ilea's legs before she regenerates them. The mage ends the confrontation and asks the Hand to take charge of Cless, a young girl found in the ruin. Cless says she is from London and is searching for her doctor father, making her another apparent arrival from Earth. Claire assumes responsibility for her while concealing that connection. The team explores farther, but a collapse buries the deeper dungeon entrance.

Ilea establishes a concealed home near Ravenhall and grows closer to Kyrian. He reveals that he survived street life and exploited child labor, admits his limited literacy, and accepts Ilea's help learning to read. Ilea entrusts him with her Earth origin, though their brief intimacy leaves him hurt and confused when she does not want a committed relationship. Meanwhile, a covert Hand operative finishes a network of runes intended to undermine the guild. The plot erupts during the Hand tournament as demons pour into the training area and reach Viscera. Ilea fights through the incursion and reunites with Trian, but they cannot reach the rest of Team 34 before a vast portal opens. A colossal creature emerges, and the defending elder engages it. Ilea and Trian are swept through the rift into a dark ocean realm with no visible route back, while the fates of Claire, Eve, Kyrian, Cless, and Ravenhall remain unknown to them.

Stranded in the Great Salt, Ilea tells Trian about Earth and introduces him to Aki. The pair bargain with a sapient Mind Weaver that wants to escape its violent realm. Their wary alliance leads them to an ancient steel facility operated through unfamiliar runes and lightning. Ilea names the demon Weavy. Inside, they confront the Shadow's Hand elder responsible for the rifts, who claims the invasion was meant to test and strengthen the guild. He summons monsters, uses the facility's controls, and disappears, leaving the three allies amid competing demon forces. After surviving, they discover that the central device can display and target distant places. One view appears to offer Ilea a route to Earth, but she chooses the life and people she has in Elos. She focuses the device on her hidden home and has Trian activate it. Elsewhere, Kyrian keeps Cless alive near demon-held Ravenhall and finds the city still burning under Mind Weaver control.

Ilea, Trian, and Weavy return to her mountain home, where Kyrian and Cless have taken refuge. Ilea identifies the saboteur as Adam Strand and learns that Ravenhall has fallen while Claire and Eve are missing. Weavy joins the survivors as a provisional ally and helps Sulivhaan's squad clear demon groups around the city. The combined force retakes Morhill, attracting the attention of Imperial scouts. Eve, alive in Virilya, continues a separate covert investigation and survives a battle that yields new leads. Ilea travels to Virilya and finds Dagon organizing the surviving Shadow's Hand. After hearing Ilea's account of Adam, Dagon summons the guild to Ravenhall, and more than a hundred members answer. Dagon and Sulivhaan prepare the counterattack while scouts identify many Mind Weavers controlling the occupation. Ilea, Trian, Kyrian, and Weavy enter the sewer route beneath Ravenhall with Weavy's controlled demons, beginning the effort to break the city's defenses from within.

The Shadow's Hand attacks Ravenhall while Ilea and other infiltrators hunt the Mind Weavers directing its defenders. Each leader they kill destabilizes more demons, but a powerful winged demon nearly overwhelms Ilea and escapes south. A fresh rift releases two enormous creatures. One dies when the rift closes through it, while the other, Bane of the Deep, devastates the battlefield with sound. Ilea enters the creature, destroys its organs, and secures the level-823 kill. With the command structure broken, the Hand contains the remaining horde. Weavy proves his allegiance by destroying his own controlled spawn rather than leave them as a danger. Ilea reunites with Trian and Kyrian at a newly formed lake that sends demon spawn into the Hand's training area and will require permanent guards. After days of fighting through streets and underground passages, the Hand clears Ravenhall. The surviving defenders begin disposing of the dead and repairing the walls.

Dagon and Sulivhaan secure Imperial cooperation in Ravenhall's reconstruction and a stronger governing role for the Shadow's Hand. Ilea finds Claire and her unresponsive mother pursued by Dawntree hunters seeking information about Alice. Ilea identifies herself as Lilith and kills the hunters after learning they drove Claire from safety and attacked during her escape. Claire remains with the Hand, is hired into Ravenhall's new administration, and takes Cless as her assistant and ward. Trian gives Claire his drawings of the Great Salt runes, then prepares to check on his family as reports confirm demon attacks far beyond Ravenhall. Eve's investigation links the Golden Lily to Trian's family. She kills a poison druid in Virilya but leaves the battle critically wounded, bleeding, and without healing supplies, making her immediate survival uncertain. Weavy remains distrusted despite his service. Ilea departs toward Riverwatch with Kyrian and Weavy, while Adam Strand, the escaped winged demon, the spawn lake, the Golden Lily, and the mysteries of Earth travel remain unresolved.

characters.description: The narrator of this novella, a member of the White Court of vampires, who feed on human emotion. Handsome, sardonic, and privately haunted by his predatory nature, he has spent years secretly watching over and protecting the wizard Harry Dresden, his half-brother, often without Harry's knowledge. He walks a hard line between the monstrous demands of his blood and his fierce loyalty to the people he loves.
characters.name: Thomas Raith

characters.description: Chicago's professional wizard and a private investigator who handles supernatural cases. Powerful, stubborn, and quick to charge into danger to help others, he is the person Thomas is determined to protect in this story, largely from behind the scenes and without Harry realizing the full extent of the threat around him.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: Thomas's sister and the true guiding power behind the White Court of vampires, coldly intelligent and dangerously seductive. She manages the family's interests with ruthless political skill, and her aims and Thomas's do not always align.
characters.name: Lara Raith

recaps.ending: Thomas succeeds in protecting Harry from the danger closing around him without ever revealing the existence of the Oblivion War. Harry survives the night largely unaware of how close the threat came or of the hidden conflict his brother is bound to. The secret of the war is preserved, Thomas's loyalties remain concealed, and the quiet, one-sided vigilance he keeps over his brother continues as it did before.
recaps.in_short: Told from the point of view of Thomas Raith, this novella follows him as he works to protect his half-brother, the wizard Harry Dresden, from a danger Harry cannot be allowed to learn about. Thomas is secretly part of the Oblivion War, an ancient, hidden effort to erase the names of certain old and terrible beings from human memory so they can never again be called into the world. Harry has stumbled unknowingly into the edges of this war, drawing the attention of a faction that wants to exploit what he has touched. Because the rules of the war forbid revealing it to outsiders, Thomas must guard Harry without telling him what is truly at stake, maneuvering alone against supernatural enemies. Through a night of danger he manages to shield his brother and blunt the threat, keeping both the secret and Harry intact.

recaps.text: The Dresden Files follow Harry Dresden, Chicago's professional wizard. Among his closest ties is Thomas Raith, a member of the White Court of vampires, who feed on human emotion. Thomas has spent years secretly helping Harry from the shadows and shielding him from dangers Harry never learns of, hiding both his hunger and the true depth of their bond as half-brothers. The White Court is a family of predators governed through cold politics, and Thomas is caught between his monstrous nature and his loyalty to the brother he has chosen to protect.

characters.description: A large and powerful man who appears with both legs broken and bound to a stretcher aboard a helicopter. Three men cut him loose and force him through the open door over remote desert country, apparently murdering him.
characters.name: Calvin Franz

characters.description: The pilot who flies the helicopter carrying Calvin Franz and three other men into remote desert country. He holds the aircraft in a high hover while the passengers force Franz through the open door.
characters.name: Helicopter pilot

characters.description: A former Army military policeman who travels without a fixed address or planned destination. Nearly out of money in Portland, he recognizes an unexpected $1,030 bank deposit as an old urgent-assistance signal and sets out to identify the sender.
characters.name: Jack Reacher

characters.description: The sender of the coded $1,030 deposit that summons Jack Reacher. She is a capable former colleague whose difficult and expensive way of reaching him convinces him that her request is urgent, although the nature of the emergency is not yet known.
characters.name: Frances Neagley

characters.description: Calvin Franz's contact during the opening inquiry into his disappearance. The sheriff's department encourages her to approach Frances Neagley, a step intended to draw Franz's former special-investigations colleagues into examining the case.
characters.name: Angela Franz

characters.description: A former member of Jack Reacher's special investigations unit with financial expertise. She studies Calvin Franz's seven months of spreadsheets and calculates that their worsening results contain 650 excess failures, matching a separate $65 million clue.
characters.name: Karla Dixon

characters.description: A former special-investigations member who later worked at New Age Defense Systems. He met Franz, Sanchez, and Orozco shortly before the disappearances, but New Age says it recently dismissed him and destroyed his computer drive under company procedure.
characters.name: Tony Swan

characters.description: A former special-investigations member and Las Vegas security operator. He joined Franz, Swan, and Orozco at a meeting shortly before the disappearances, and a note from his apartment records 650 units at $100,000 each.
characters.name: Jorge Sanchez

characters.description: A former special-investigations member and Jorge Sanchez's partner in a Las Vegas security business. He attended the meeting with Sanchez, Franz, and Swan shortly before the disappearances and is consequently part of the inquiry into the unexplained 650-unit transaction.
characters.name: Manuel Orozco

characters.description: A Los Angeles County sheriff who supervises Thomas Brant and is conducting an independent investigation into the former unit members' deaths and disappearances. He confirms their recent meeting and supplies Sanchez's note about a $65 million transaction.
characters.name: Curtis Mauney

characters.description: A Los Angeles County sheriff's deputy serving under Curtis Mauney. After an earlier fight with Jack Reacher, Brant attempts to retaliate, but Mauney intervenes and stops him while the investigation into the missing former unit members continues.
characters.name: Thomas Brant

characters.description: A human-resources representative at New Age Defense Systems. She tells the investigators that Tony Swan was dismissed more than three weeks earlier and that his computer drive was physically destroyed under the company's strict paperless security rules.
characters.name: Margaret Berenson

characters.description: A former special-investigations member working alongside Jack Reacher in the field. When two armed men attack them in Hollywood, O'Donnell helps disarm and incapacitate the assailants, then joins the pursuit of the investigation's Las Vegas connection.
characters.name: David O'Donnell

characters.description: A staffer for a member of the House Defense Committee who can access restricted information about Little Wing, New Age Defense Systems' classified product. A coded response from Frances Neagley's Pentagon contact identifies her as the investigators' next government contact.
characters.name: Diana Bond

characters.description: A traveller using four identities that appear together on an unofficial Homeland Security watch list. Records place one of those identities in New York and another en route to Las Vegas, but his purpose and any connection to the former unit members' deaths remain unknown.
characters.name: Azhari Mahmoud

characters.description: A former FBI agent who manages security for a Las Vegas casino. He knew Sanchez and Orozco through their work for smaller casinos and directs Jack Reacher's group to Milena, a woman who was close to Sanchez.
characters.name: Wright

characters.description: A worker at the Fire Pit bar and Jorge Sanchez's longtime on-and-off partner. She recognizes the former unit members because Sanchez had told her that they would come if he was ever in trouble, making her a direct lead in the search for him.
characters.name: Milena

characters.description: Manuel Orozco's wife and the mother of their three children. She explains that Orozco and Sanchez had no active clients, and that their sudden assignment began when a former Army colleague in California appealed to them for help.
characters.name: Tammy Orozco

characters.description: The name on the wallet carried by a dark-blue-suited gunman who attacks the investigators in Las Vegas. The man uses a shell-company vehicle, and his phone records connect him to an unidentified superior in Los Angeles.
characters.name: Seropian

characters.description: A lower-ranking New Age Defense Systems guard named in the company directory. The investigators identify him as the man found dead after the Las Vegas attack, whose wallet carried the name Seropian.
characters.name: Saropian

characters.description: New Age Defense Systems' security chief and a former LAPD robbery-homicide officer. He is the Los Angeles superior linked to the Las Vegas attack and is identified as the organizer who used threats against employees' children to conceal the electronics scheme.
characters.name: Allen Lamaison

characters.description: New Age Defense Systems' original development engineer and current quality-control director. Allen Lamaison has apparently forced him, through threats against his daughter, to certify functioning Little Wing electronics packs as rejects.
characters.name: Edward Dean

characters.description: A former LAPD officer in the upper ranks of New Age security beneath Allen Lamaison. Margaret Berenson identifies him as one of the people aware of the scheme and as a participant in the helicopter operation.
characters.name: Lennox

characters.description: A former LAPD officer in New Age security who serves beneath Allen Lamaison. Margaret Berenson identifies him among the limited group that knows about the scheme and says he took part in the helicopter operation.
characters.name: Parker

recaps.ending: Jack Reacher hides aboard Allen Lamaison's helicopter and intervenes as Lamaison's associates prepare to throw Karla Dixon and David O'Donnell from the aircraft. He frees both captives, sends the two associates out of the helicopter, kills Lamaison, and later kills the pilot after forcing a landing at Edward Dean's remote home. Azhari Mahmoud arrives expecting Dean to demonstrate how to arm the stolen Little Wing systems. Reacher and Frances Neagley capture Mahmoud, restrain the arriving truck driver, and alert a Pentagon contact. Federal authorities take control of Mahmoud, the missile shipment, and the evidence before any of the 650 systems are armed. Dixon administers the recovered financial instruments and diamonds, establishing support for the victims' families, Tony Swan's dog charity, expenses, and the surviving investigators. Reacher, Neagley, Dixon, and O'Donnell separate at LAX. Weeks later, Dixon deposits Reacher's $111,822.18 share in his account. The amount encodes both mission accomplished and her Greenwich Village ZIP code, leaving him an invitation while he continues travelling. The final dispositions of Curtis Mauney, Lennox, and Parker are unstated.
recaps.in_short: After Calvin Franz is murdered, Frances Neagley summons Jack Reacher and reunites him with former special-investigations colleagues Karla Dixon and David O'Donnell. Their search links the deaths of Franz, Tony Swan, Jorge Sanchez, and Manuel Orozco to New Age Defense Systems. Security chief Allen Lamaison has coerced employees into falsely rejecting 650 working electronics packs for Little Wing missiles and arranged their sale to Azhari Mahmoud. Sheriff Curtis Mauney is exposed as Lamaison's partner, while Dixon and O'Donnell are captured. Reacher boards the conspirators' helicopter, rescues them, and kills Lamaison. Reacher and Neagley then capture Mahmoud before the missile shipment can be armed for attacks in the United States. Federal authorities receive the prisoner, shipment, and evidence. The recovered assets support the victims' families, Tony Swan's dog charity, expenses, and the surviving investigators. The four survivors separate, and Dixon later sends Reacher his share with a coded invitation to Greenwich Village.

recaps.text: Previously, Jack Reacher served as an Army military policeman and led a special investigations unit. After leaving the Army, he lived as a drifter, carrying little and travelling without a fixed address, a phone, or a planned destination.

Calvin Franz is carried by helicopter into remote desert country with both legs broken and his body strapped to a stretcher. Three men cut him free and force him from the aircraft while it hovers thousands of feet above the ground. Seventeen days later, Jack Reacher is nearly out of money in Portland, Oregon, when he discovers an unexplained $1,030 deposit in his bank account. He interprets the amount as 1030, an urgent-assistance code used by Army military police. The bank traces the personal check to Frances Neagley. Reacher remembers recruiting Neagley into his special investigations unit, where she became central to its success. Because she is highly capable and intensely private, he concludes that she would use such an indirect method only for a serious emergency. Reacher calls her Chicago security company. An assistant says Neagley is flying to Los Angeles, wants him there immediately, and expects him to locate her on arrival. The assistant also confirms that Neagley is trying to reach several people and that Reacher is the first to answer. Reacher commits to the trip without yet knowing what has alarmed her.

The inquiry connects Calvin Franz, Tony Swan, Jorge Sanchez, and Manuel Orozco through a meeting shortly before their disappearances. Karla Dixon finds that Franz's seven months of performance records contain 650 excess failures. Sanchez left a matching calculation: 650 units at $100,000 each, totaling $65 million. New Age Defense Systems says it recently dismissed Swan and destroyed his computer drive, while the purpose of the figures remains unknown. Manuel Orozco is then identified as another victim apparently dropped from a helicopter. A Pentagon contact names New Age's classified product as Little Wing and directs the group to congressional staffer Diana Bond. Records from Sanchez and Orozco's office link Azhari Mahmoud to four travelling identities. Two are Adrian Mount and Andrew MacBride; the others are Alan Mason and Anthony Matthews. After two gunmen attack Reacher and David O'Donnell in Hollywood, the investigators follow a possible Las Vegas lead. Casino security manager Wright directs them to Milena, Sanchez's longtime partner. Milena and Tammy Orozco explain that the men's failing business suddenly received work after Franz called from California asking for help. A further Las Vegas attacker carries the name Seropian, and his phone connects him to an unidentified Los Angeles superior. The group returns to Los Angeles to pursue that link and learn what Little Wing is.

Diana Bond identifies Little Wing as a shoulder-launched surface-to-air missile. Its Los Angeles electronics production ran normally for three months before rising numbers of units supposedly failed quality control and were destroyed. Combining this information with Franz's records, the team concludes that 650 working packs were falsely rejected for sale to Azhari Mahmoud. A matching group of missile bodies is scheduled for false destruction, creating a route for complete weapons to leave Colorado. Tony Swan is confirmed dead, making clear that Franz, Swan, Sanchez, and Orozco were killed after investigating the diversion. Documents taken from New Age identify its real plant in Highland Park and name security chief Allen Lamaison as the Los Angeles superior behind the attackers. Margaret Berenson explains that Lamaison threatened Edward Dean's daughter to make the quality-control director falsify records, then threatened her son to enforce her silence. She identifies Lennox, Parker, and Saropian as other participants. Reacher and Frances Neagley move Berenson and her son to safety. Soon afterward, the missile shipment leaves Colorado, while Lamaison's group captures Dixon and O'Donnell. Their encoded proof-of-life answers signal that eight enemies are present, including Curtis Mauney. Reacher and Neagley penetrate the Highland Park plant, kill four guards, and confront Mauney, who admits he is Lamaison's partner. The captives remain in immediate danger as Reacher and Neagley leave the grounds temporarily to regain mobility.

At the airfield, Jack Reacher kills the man guarding him, draws the pursuing cars away, and secretly boards the conspirators' Bell helicopter. Allen Lamaison's group brings the bound Karla Dixon and David O'Donnell aboard. When two armed associates prepare to throw the captives from the hovering aircraft, Reacher shoots one man out, forces the other to fall, frees his colleagues, and kills Lamaison in the same manner. The team concludes that Azhari Mahmoud plans to use the 650 Little Wing systems inside the United States and must rely on Edward Dean, the only engineer able to assemble and test them. Reacher forces the helicopter to Dean's remote home and kills the pilot, who admits participating in the earlier murders. Dean acknowledges falsifying 650 electronics records under coercion. Mahmoud arrives expecting an assembly demonstration and confirms that the missiles are in transit for domestic attacks. Reacher and Frances Neagley capture him, and Neagley calls a Pentagon contact. Federal authorities take custody of Mahmoud, the shipment, and the evidence before any missiles are armed. Dixon converts the recovered financial instruments and diamonds into support for the victims' families, Tony Swan's dog charity, expenses, and shares for the survivors. Reacher, Neagley, Dixon, and O'Donnell separate at LAX. Weeks later, Dixon deposits Reacher's share with a numerical message that marks the mission complete and invites him to Greenwich Village.
